You'll see a lot of people recommending this game based off of the art, while warning those who expect an FPS game to stay away. And yes, that is definitely true. But if you're expecting an atmospheric game with puzzles and environmental mechanics that rival those of Myst (like I was after the game began to present itself that way), you'll also be sorely disappointed.

At its core, Scorn is only here to look pretty and interesting. It definitely wholesale leans into Giger's aesthetic, and that's cool. But the game is a glorified walking sim with a handful of puzzles and some oddly placed combat that arrives towards the back end, all of which can be completed in around 3.5-5 hours from what I've seen after refunding it. It's not worth the asking price of $40 in my opinion, as its severe lack of gameplay makes it something I'd be a lot more comfortable paying $15 max for.

I went in expecting nothing, but the problem is that the game really built up expectations in its first 30 minutes or so. With a series like Myst (or Obduction), which is an experience near and dear to my heart, there's heaps of storytelling to be discovered as you progress through the games' puzzles. There are loads of intricate environmental details that you can interact with directly and immerse yourself in. Scorn only has the vaguest of story lines, and much less environmental mechanics to interact with and discover than I would like.

There's definitely an audience for Scorn, and if you loved the game, then that's awesome. But to me, it's very overpriced for a game that had way more potential than it delivered. It's worth noting that the game IS on Game Pass currently though, if you have that. And I'd say it's a great game to check out there as part of your subscription.

Scorn as a game involves two main segments, a slow paced trek through a Gigerian Nightmare, solving puzzles and wondering if the sculpture on the wall is supposed to represent the fear of intercourse or the damaging effect of growing up and realizing your parents really did have sex. The art itself is very nice to look at but just a lot all around, the middle portion of the game particular being where you'll find yourself cross-eyed and forgetting whether the path with the phallic tendril going into the egg was the way you came from or the way you're supposed to go. The puzzles are alright, they're never too much of a head scratcher, and if you're struggling with one you just have to remember you only have to do it two more times. Every puzzle in this game adheres to the rule of 3's. Every. Single. One. Some areas have you spending minutes upon minutes walking back and forth up and down halls to repeat what you've done once and twice now.

The second segment of gameplay is combat, to make it short, the combat is not good. There are 3 Schlongs in this world, that you'll fight over and over. They'll despawn or stop attacking if you walk past certain thresholds in the map. The weapons never seem to have enough ammo, which results in encounters approaching tedium as your pistol runs out of spunk and there's always one more Weiner that you'll have to duke it out with the Melee Penetrator that comes with 2 hits and takes 5 seconds to use again after, and no, you cannot use the Penetrator 3 times if you take a week break between goes. There's a healing system that's just flat out not shown to you unless you open up the settings and look at the controls. There's an Organ constantly rearranging your insides that burns one of said heals every time he digs a little deeper. The saving grace of the combat is that it ends, jokes aside, you're only fighting off Todgers for a short 1 and half period of a 4-6 hour game.  Leave it to the Bollocks. Dong.

In short, if you can get past the mediocre gameplay and enjoy the art design for what it is, yes buy it but for most people there are 100 games that may not look as good. But you'll feel better after playing.

What I call 'brutes'. And what do Brutes NOT do...?

b) you shoot your gun, thus making noise

Scorn is a gory, alien body horror first person puzzle game heavily inspired by HR Giger's art.

Even though HR Giger is my favorite artist and this game seems to be tailor made for me, there is still no getting around it: Scorn is a BAD game. The TLDR is that the art is good, even great at times, but the gameplay is frustrating and mediocre, and the story telling muddled and confused, all of it often working against the whole.

The primary reason why I cannot recommend Scorn is that you spend a lot of time confused and lost, but not in a good way. While it could be fun to explore strange alien architecture, you instead usually hunt around the sprawling levels looking for the next interact-able object. You are looking for the video game piece to progress so you aren't looking at the pretty and detailed scenery. Because everything is so alien, the gameplay trains you to find things you can walk up to just see if the little interact-ability circle pops up. Not only is this boring and frustrating, it also makes you actively miss all that surrounds you. 

The game is really, really bad at telling you what it wants you to do to the point where I believe its a deliberate design decision. Branching paths, things circling back on themselves, events that seem nonsensical... it all makes you wonder what you are actually supposed to do. I think the idea was to force players to spend more time around the lush environments, but since I am running around with the purpose of progressing and the environments are NOT linked to that progress, you don't actually end up looking at it. I started the game taking my time, admiring the strange and grotesque artwork, but once I started encountering puzzles and play elements, I spent less and less time looking at the art. 

And it is art. The one thing this game has going for it, is of course the Gigeresque creatures and levels. And they are gorgeous. Brutal, sickening, yet sometimes alluring. And above all else, alien. Though of course the alien design doesn't help the gameplay at all because you can't identify what anything is really supposed to do. Its beautiful but not functional in a game.

That is the crux of the problem. The gameplay is actively bad and, on top of that, draws you away from the art, and the art doesn't help the gameplay at all either. And the isolated parts, like the puzzles and combat, are really simple and not much fun. I want to make clear, that especially for a game like this, it does not HAVE to be fun, it can bring something else to the table... but I do not think it does bring anything else to the table.

Also, just to make sure it is said, there is not much of a "story" here. There is no dialogue or text, but you could still tell a story through environmental storytelling. But Scorn somehow manages to flub this too. Things do happen but they don't really make sense. You are in a crumbling, seemingly forgotten facility. One of the first events encases you in some ooze, and then the facility is even more crumbling and more forgotten? Not sure what the takeaway is supposed to be. Which would be fine if there was some sort of emotional takeaway, but the game doesn't have a deft hand there either. Your character goes through some painful scenes, being horribly injected and the like, but its impossible to relate to your character so all those scenes fall flat. Your character takes punishment far beyond what a human could survive and continually does things no human would do or even think to do. Encounter a strange alien polyp device? Yeah, inject its fluid straight into my wrist, sure, why not. So all those scenes where our character takes a moment to look at the "strange" gun they just picked up don't work, because the things they treat as strange are no more strange than the things they treat as normal. Pulling out a tentacled umbilical chord really loses its punch when I both do not know how painful it is or if its even weird for the character. And because the facility is in disrepair and overgrown with strange alien stuff, but also some of the strange alien stuff is part of the machinery, its often impossible to tell what is a sign of decay, what is functioning as its supposed to, or what is supposed to be an invasive foreign entity. We have alien things interacting with alien things in alien ways, with not nearly enough context to get anything out of it.

Scorn is one of those interesting failures of a game where it is a little fun to pull at the strings and try to figure out why its a failure. I could write more about this game, even kind of want to. But I tell you what I do not want to do. Play more Scorn.

I've been noticing a trend in videogame storytelling in the past few years: games want to really go hard for that whole 'show, don't tell' style of storytelling. Most attempts fall flat because what they show is so vague and open to interpretation that there might as well not be a story.

This is especially relevant in case when it comes to Scorn.

Scorn is really a game about only one things: visually realizing an artists uncomfortable vision of a flesh-mechanical civilization, where every button, switch and lever is a squishy horror and entire buildings are constructed seemingly only for the purpose of inflicting torment and suffering. If a story exists in this game, it is left so vague and so unclear as to not exist at all. Why places exist, why we move through them, why we interact with them, why we fight against fleshy blobmonsters or why the game ends with such an underwhelming whimper of the developer displaying their deep discomfort with sexuality, we will never know.

Scorn is very, very pretty, though. The only reason it ever got off the ground and got attention is its visual and technical production. Borrowing from a few disturbing art sources for inspiration, it creates a truly impressive visual parade of horrors. Machines, rooms, passages, long-dead creatures, even the very weapons the player carries are all designed and realized with such meticulous detail it's a wonder the developer ever completed their project.

Sadly, I fear it is that attention to visual detail and rich animation of gore and flesh that left the rest of the game so utterly failing to be playable. Scorn has perhaps four or five simple puzzles, and each of those are repeated a standard set of three times to pad out the game. It has maybe four or five enemy types, which are repeated ad nauseam. It gives you four weapons, very limited ammo and a combat system that is frustratingly slow, clunky and unfun to play with. Its very visual style fight against any attempt to create a game in this setting, as the rooms and tunnels begin to melt together in the player's mind for looking too similar, as navigation becomes a chore and as the prolonged animations drag on to turn even the most simple actions, such as moving an elevator, into sheer suffering to wait through.

Scorn, then, is a game that manages to intrigue for its first half hour, and for about another fifteen minutes towards the very end. Between those times there are a few hours of horribly underdeveloped gameplay, wasted time and repetition that leaves me wholly unable to recommend this game. If you want to get all the best parts of Scorn without having to suffer through its content, you can just watch someone else do a longplay of it on Youtube. You'll see all the pretty and strange and disturbing things without having to waste your own time or money.

[h1] 🫀 Scorn  [/h1]
Gore, veins, and wasted potential

[h2]Intro[/h2]
[i] Scorn is a game I honestly never thought I’d play. I’ve got a vein phobia and this game is basically nothing but veins and organic nightmares. I took it as a challenge to see how long I could last in its grotesque world… and somehow I ended up finishing it 100%.

Now comes the question: would I recommend it? Not really. Only if you’re obsessed with grim atmosphere, unique art direction, megalophobia vibes, and the feeling of wandering alone through a disturbing, alien world.[/i]

[h2]World & Atmosphere - The one and only[/h2]

This is where Scorn shines the most. The organic modular weapons, the grotesque and hyper-detailed environments — there’s really nothing else like it on the market. The world design is disgusting yet fascinating, and the audio adds constant unease with creepy ambient noises.

The downside? [b]It’s all style and very little substance.[/b]

[h2] Gameplay – Slow, clunky, tedious [/h2]

The whole thing lasts maybe 4–5 hours. Most of it is just walking back and forth to complete puzzles. The combat? Honestly, a joke. Slow, clunky, repetitive, unpolished.

Some sections feel like pure filler, added only to drag out the game instead of making it meaningful.

[h2] Music & Sound - Eerie and good[/h2]

The audio design is one of the few flawless parts. The soundtrack and ambient noises constantly send chills down your spine. Easily one of the highlights.

[h2] Story – Art or nonsense? [/h2]

The story is mediocre at best. The ending is far from satisfying, and a lot of it feels like bad filler. Spoiler alert: [spoiler]at the end, you end up in an area full of statues having sex in random positions. Like… was that really necessary? It’s pure cringe. You also briefly control two other characters, but it’s barely used at all — wasted potential for something much more interesting.[/spoiler]

[h2] Achievements - Mediocre grind [/h2]

Achievements are as plain as it gets. Just finish the game and that’s basically it. No creative challenges, no speedruns, nothing memorable. Another wasted opportunity.

[h2] Conclusion [/h2]

Scorn is a visually and audibly unique experience, but that’s all it has going for it. The atmosphere is haunting, but the gameplay is shallow, the story underwhelming, and the ending straight-up cringe. I can’t recommend a game just for its aesthetic vibe.

Sorn is a beautiful crafted game and was truly a blessing to play. The  and unique environments, buildings, and themes were something to behold and will stick with me forever. In fact, I personally don't usually leave reviews recommending or not for games because each person's experience with a game will be different. Not to mention that the story and themes of that story of every game will always speak to each person differently due to their own experiences and view.
However, despite this I feel like I need to leave one for Scorn, as this game while being a wonderful and fantasti game it is also a game I cannot with any conscience recommend to another player to buy with their money in this current economic environment, especially when we have so many games that are stealing the stoplight due to their amazing achievement. Don't get me wrong this game is definitely a one of a kind but it is incredibly short, I beat the game start to finish with all the achievements except for one in only 4.2 hours. That means that at full price $40, you are paying $10 for each hour almost. I got it for half off ($20) and still feel like it wasn't worth it despite that really is the only reasonable price for the game.It's because of this that I usually do not buy games from small teams or companies that are not trip A studios. Not to discredit the team that made this game, as they definitely deserve praise for making such an amazing game and I truly believe that an incredible game such as this one could have never been made by a trip A/big studio due to it's mature themes, buildings, "story", and creatures and I am not just talking about the blood and gore; therefore, I commend this team in making this game and would love to recommend it to friends, family, and strangers. However, for the reasons that I will get into besides just the length of this game, I cannot.Starting with the combat, while it is certainly unique and different from most games that does not necessarily mean it's a compliment. In fact at the start of the game I recommend completely avoiding combat at all costs as if anything it will slow you down and annoy you more than anything. The first gun you get in the game in punishing and has a range that is hard and confusing to read much like classic COD Zombies "knifing" before they fixed it later generations. Except in this case in addition to having confusion on the range, if you miss or hit you are forced to go through a short cool-down before you can fire this flesh piston again into the enemy.I am sure this was created with the best of intentions to seemly make tease combat situations where you think about your health and ammo when you get "guns" that require it later, which I will speak on later in this review in their own respective places; however, instead it creates this situations that feel unfair, frustrating, and down right bullshit. Which is why even after I got the ranged weapons throughout the game I avoided combat at every opportunity I could which could even how I manage to beat the game so quickly. My intention was never to "speedrun" this game the issue is that even once you get range weapons the combat is way to punishing.As in they only give you enough ammo to fight every scenario exactly without missing, which combined with dying and the save system (which I will speak on later) makes this game down right rage inducing and there were several times I just simply quit the game as it wasn't worth continuing in the slightest knowing that these same issues were going to be present throughout the entire game. The only reason I would continue was simply to continue to enjoy the amazing scenery and to see where this story would go. That being said, I love discovering each of the "guns" and loved out original and amazing each one was, as well as I was impressed with the "inventory system" and the animation for switching "guns" and for seeing how much ammo and blood (which works as a potion to restore your health) was left.The real issue is that because the ammo is limited that missing a station for health or ammo because it's tucked around a corner is a death sentence and combining this with the games saving and death, downright makes it again too punishing and makes the issue a glaring red-flag that you will be reminded of throughout the game time and time again. Not mention enemies don't drop anything, no ammo or health making your character effectively a masochist and giving the player literally no incentive to participate in combat unless obviously necessary to continue with the story and/or to complete a puzzle. Which quick tip, I found that enemies will leave you alone while you are doing puzzles. I only found this out because of how "nails against a chalkboard" the combat was and this resulted in an endless loop where I would kite/ignore/run-past enemies get to the obvious puzzle->complete it->get out of the animation and lead the enemies out of a corridor->dodge enemies and run to the next section.Which is why I constantly avoided combat; however, that being said the moments outside of combat, even the small sections between combat was downright fantastic! All the puzzles were intuitive to a degree I have not seen in a game before. I am talking about being about to understand what to do without any hints or guides, but still being hard enough that it gives you a fair challenge and some moments of failing only to understand what the game is asking of you and getting it immediately or after a couple more times. Which is honestly an impressive feat and something the devs should be praised for, for sure! This cause and effect with lack of rewards from the combat, limited ammo/health, and puzzle all wouldn't such an issue if death and saving in this game weren't what was holding this game back so much.
Death in this game is the kind of torture of having each finger nail painfully and slowly being pulled off each finger which aptly fits into this games theme so maybe that was the point! *jokingly* It is the same in that one the first nail has been ripped off it sucks, but you think to yourself, "At least it's over" only to see them move to the next finger to start the process all over again. This being that there are several story related animations that occur while moving from each section that I will not spoil that happen, which by themselves are incredible and a sight to behold! The problem is that since all saving is all automatic and not controlled by the player at all that once you die sometimes you have to watch these scenes over and over again because you die because you missed a single shot, didn't know what to do, activated a puzzle/story piece too early (this one really only an issue towards the end as most things can't be done out of order as the game wont let you), etc.Which is what ruins what are otherwise some of the coolest *cutscenes*/animations I have seen in a game in such a long time. This also bleeds back into the combat issues I have discussed eariler about missing hidden stations for ammo/health as when the game does auto save (and it does this without telling you) it saves your health and ammo you have left exactly as they are. So if you think you could do a combat encounter or boss battle better after you know what to do, well the game says, "fuck you, git gud scrub." Except unlike a game such as Dark souls it saves seemly at random not always after important animation, events, progression which makes it again super frustrating and has a feeling of being down right unfair. It's such a simple fix too if you are going to do this or have a game feel tense let the players save and load at their own discretion. Could you imagine if it saved your health and how many estus flasks you had before got to the boss door and not being able to refill them until you beat the boss? Being forced to watch the boss cut-scene or animation without being able skip it every single time? There's more but I'll say this free on gamepass

This is a game absolutely worth buying if it's on sale. It has a lot of positive things going for it. But, ultamitly what is there is not worth playing if you're here for a game. This is meant to be looked at from the perspective of it's a painting and not much else, as you won't find much else.

Firstly the story is that of a fevered dream. It's hard to grasp and understand the world around you as you blindly blunder about killing whatever moves. The absolutely stunning artwork has absolutely no sense of reason why it should be there with what silent story they're trying to tell. It feels like a mess of ideas and concepts that were all glued without thought, when the demo all those years ago clearly showed plenty of it.

Combat is a complete joke. Your first weapon is a dinky short range rod, which seems like the devs telling you that combat is not worth doing and is best avoided. But, that intuition is null and void when they spawn loads of monsters in your way without a alternative route or trap to get rid of them. The game forces you into every confrontation you don't get a say in the matter. So, you spend all your ammo and health murdering everything in your way without a care about the world or biosphere. Plus, even if you do avoid the fight the game doesn't reward you, you don't get any more ammo or health. Nor are you rewarded for killing so why even have them there in the first place? By this point I've long been taken out of any and all immersion to believe that creatures actually live here. And at some-point a giant monster starts spawning that can't be found in the structures these things create further killing your immersion as you can't help but wonder how the hell this monstrosity got there without the devs just deciding that it does.

The ending, I really hate and really love the ending. As everything I've said so far doesn't apply, kind of. The art starts telling a cohesive story about your environment and why. Your actions start making sense as everything is better staged and choreographed, it's still a senseless fever dream but it's a start. The parasite that attached it's self to you is no longer there so the UI is gone, that UI being gone is one of the greatest things they did. As now there isn't anything telling you that you are necessarily in a game, you can now actually buy into the idea that you are this person that's been thrown into this hopeless world. And the art really makes you feel like you belong here in this part of the game as now you don't have a HUD anymore. But, this only happens at the very end at the end of the end of the game. Which is a crying shame. 

And at the very end were you see what might have happened to everyone, where they might have gone. The game enters into a cut scene, which is something I hate but anyway, the parasite randomly decides to come back. It somehow knew right where you to kill the moment you were having with all this wonder and discovery it forces it's self on you fuses with you and makes you into a lump of flesh for absolutely zero reasons! And then you get a screen shot of the thing you wanted to explore with your now fused fleshy bit in the middle of it, thus ending the game. This is awful! It feels like you had concept art for that scene and felt like you had to use it and morphed the entire game around it. Because the whole parasite thing is, well really fun, but your execution of it deranges anyone trying to get to know your world. I haven't felt like I understood anything about Scorn. There is clearly a social structure but whatever it is it can't be liner as you find humanoids in walnuts (greatest literal pun ever by the way), people growing from walls outside the main (?) structure but can't be found inside but in one scene, another grows from flowers inside the structure, and who knows if the creatures you find derping around are human--the big momma certainly must be, someone what. 

Now, I have to say it but this version of Scorn is nothing like the demo. I would rather play the demo again, because it has the same problems the full release does, mainly combat, while having all the wanna be features the Kickstarter promised. As the world was suppose to be expressive with how you interacted with it was supposed to effect it and it you, anyway what is done is dead.

Overall, if you're here for art and art alone it's a solid buy. Totally worth it if you have money to burn or if it's on sale, but if you were here for the world and immersion you're out of luck. Maybe they'll remake it or re-release it, and I really hope they do. As the ideas they have are far from being bad, except the ending that was bad.

The weapons themselves are actually fine and I think feel pretty good in isolation, but they're just not in a sandbox where they can shine.

Ultimately, you can buy the art book and witness the artistry of these guys at a much better pace - that is, at your *own* pace - with no distractingly convoluted level design, annoying enemy encounters, or nonsensical mechanics to draw you out of the experience. And I do think you should support these developers one way or another, because art like this is once in a generation and I would hate to not see more like it. I just think the medium of art is sometimes as important to consider as the art itself.

I backed Scorn back in 2017 during the Kickstarter campaign, a few years later or maybe three i got access to the alpha demo. 

I really loved what I saw, but being an alpha, there were a few things that felt lacking. Granted, this was a small slice, but the core mechanics that made it into the full release were all there.

So I was sad to see that the combat aspects of the game really didn't evolve during that timespan. It was clunky, and didn't feel great during the alpha, and sadly this is what we got in the full release.

I really love the look, the feel of the world, the sounds, the music. It's all great stuff. But the combat encounters are just frustrating to the point where i kind of just wish there would be no combat at all.

I get that the game probably needed some suspension of some sort, but maybe there could have been some other element, instead of relying on "guns".

And maybe combat wouldn't have been so bad if the checkpoints weren't so messed up as well. Dying to do small sections over again, not to mention seeing the same slow animations (that were cool the first time) just gets exhausting.

The puzzles were nice for the most part, with one really annoying one, but I'm not a smart person, so maybe that was just my brain breaking itself trying to figure it out.

Overall, I have mixed feelings about the game. I do not regret backing it, and i enjoyed the game enough that i actually ended up finishing it on PC and Xbox Series X. But I'm not going to lie it's not a perfect game by any means, it's frustrating, doesn't control well and in general just mediocre.

But there are no other games out there that nail this biomechanical esthetic, and I guess that is what made my time with the game special.

Would I recommend it, no. At lest not if you are someone who gets frustrated easily. If you like me like the look of the world, maybe wait for a sale, and if you are just interested in seeing the sights and sounds, use a puzzle guide to save yourself some time.

I am...having this game on edge between a positive or negative recommendation. There are definitely things that I liked, yet around equally as much that I disliked.

Liked:
- The graphical features of the game itself. I am not talking about the content they were used for, be it the design choice for the looks of the map or the way they wanted enemies to look like. Graphics were looking nice and I cannot complain about any unpolished "that stuff glitchin'!" looks. Especially when you can view fragments from the "outside" of your usual area, the view with its lightning is looking quite fancy.
- The simple gameplay choices. For that I'm considering about the survival itself, low need of ammo management, HP management, how to approach enemies, how to get around in your current area and the rarely appearing, easy puzzles as a change.

Disliked:
- "Running in circles" being the main gameplay mechanic. I don't mind basic objectives being "do xy to access area yz" but if action xy expects me to get back to the same spot, we're not even talking about an area here, 3 to 4 times to get to progress...it certainly gives off a monotonous feeling. While this may only be true for ~half the chapters, it definitely left a mark when thinking about the game.
- The price-playtime ratio. Now...I know everyone plays at their own pace and I may not be the fella taking a look at every pixel of the environment, atleast in this case, yet I think that I spent a fair amount analyzing the environment to figure out what to do in a decent time and still got through this game too quickly. This is probably the tipping point towards the negative recommendation from my POV. 

Warning:
- This game does not treat the use of gore lightly. Its presence is available for atleast 98% of your game time in every aspect, map design, characters, enemies and probably every action you find.

TL;DR:
- Simple, enjoyable playstyle, graphics itself looking good. 
- Danger of repetitious feeling, too pricy (tipping point).
- Care for extreme use of gore if topic sensitive.

I know people have expected a lot from Scorn. Ever since the “gameplay trailer” the developers released 5 years ago, there was a lot of excitement for both the visual style and the fact that it included combat and seemed to aim at being a proper action horror game, not just a typical for the time horror themed adventure where you run away all the time. But I’ve had my reservations and the closer to release the game go, the more suspicious the trailers seemed to me so I wanted to wait and see what happens. A lukewarm reception is what happened, so I’ve decided to return to the game later, on a discount. But even that and low expectations didn’t make the experience with this game good.

It does look fantastic, of course. Although, I did have to increase the FOV and disable camera motion blur, because without the changes the game was causing a headache. But with the tweaks it looked cool, sounded alright and the overall basic idea here, for how abstract and vague it is, seemed at least promising. And apart from the fact that the game is also mercifully short, I’ve ran out of good things to say about it.

The game is mostly focused on walking and puzzle solving, which isn’t a problem in itself. But walking along a huge empty location, even when it looks pretty, gets pretty boring when you don’t have any real goal. And you don’t have any proper goals in this game apart from very short term ones. You don’t have a destination or a desire or anything, other than finding a thing that can be used and using it and then moving on until you find a next one. Even the very last moment of the game that seems to want to be dramatic is hanging completely on the fact that you’re doing what you’re doing because it’s literally the only interactive thing you can do. You don’t know why you’re doing it and why it matters, but there’s also no “I wonder what will happen”.

An approach that applies to puzzles as well, which are just there. It’s not like they are bad, it’s just that they feel sterile and tedious and the only reason you’re doing anything is because “otherwise the game won’t happen”. There’s no narrative goal to it or fun mystery in a Myst-like fashion. Occasionally the game does feature the combat that was teased in early trailers. And it’s absolute trash. It’s slow, tedious, unfun and I’ve avoided a lot of enemies not because it was “saving resources” or some tactical decision, but because it was faster and less boring. And if you die, which is quite easy, actually, or just exit the game, you might lose several dozen minutes of watching slow animations that you’ll have to do again, because the checkpointing in this game is also unreasonable and not respectful of player time.

So yeah, it’s not a good game. It’s not fun to play, being mildly amusing at rare moments, but mostly just tedious. It looks pretty so if you’re a tech artist working in Unreal Engine, maybe you can at least use this for reference. But otherwise, it’s simply not worth the little time it takes to finish and that time is better spent elsewhere.

Since I went into this with no real expectations, it managed to exceed that on some level. But what it didn't do was actually make me like it. What it succeeds at is creating an atmosphere. Graphically it's interesting and detailed. The sound design is adequately creepy and has depth. The physical elements of the world itself are well put together. If all you're looking for is to walk through a biomechanical museum of horrors, then just stop reading here and go buy the game. But if you're expecting more than that…

What it doesn't do is offer any real context or sense of accomplishment.

You wake up in a slithering world of "gross" and start sticking your hands into things, just to see what's going to get stuck on you or slither out of something controlled by whatever orifices you're interacting with. You walk through large set pieces trying to find interaction points and then engage monolithic scale puzzle elements to unlock more puzzle interaction points to make progress deeper into the moist hole of a cavern you're crawling through.

The entire experience is just a squishy nightmare of disjointed horror scenes leading to… well, that's the problem. It doesn't really lead to anything but more squishy nightmare scenes.

Personally it's not even about being scary or gross; I'm desensitized to these things which is why I don't get much out of it. I can appreciate it for the art design as a set piece. But was I supposed to be scared? Grossed out? Was I supposed to feel something by looking at these things? I need an emotional or story connection before that process can even begin and this is just the aesthetic without the meaning behind it.

It's more like the theory of a horror game without bothering to do the work of making anything in it to be actually afraid of. Why are we here? Who even is the character you're playing? Where are we going? What's the point? I'm all for a good mystery, but this isn't even offering the mystery. It's more like the developers made a big room full of scary corners, told you "hey look over there" and then just ran away without bothering to give you a pay off.

Even the difficulty doesn't come from the game being hard, it comes from the pure trial and error of exploring the world to find things that are clickable in a world full of non interactive slime. So you don't even get any real sense of accomplishment from solving things, more like relief at not having to walk in circles anymore before clicking on the next interaction. The minimal combat comes later in the game and also isn't terribly hard, more like a broader meta puzzle due to lack of ammo to cause you some urgency to move on.

Maybe in the real world if someone walked up to you and handed you the ripped off arm of an animal and walked away, you could feel actual fear of what they might do next. But when it happens in the safety of your own home, inside a video game; I'm sorry, I need more context than that before it has meaning. In the real world you might fear this potential murderer or monster of a man who just handed you body parts. In a video game you're left asking yourself, what do I do with it? Is it a puzzle piece? Do I have to fight this guy? Where is the game play from this arm? Oh, it was just a visual gag?

The context of being in a game fully removes any fear unless you actually give the player dimension and story and a reason to care. You have to get to know the character and what's going on. Nah, this just gives you stuff you're supposed to be grossed out by and then walks you to the next set piece.

From the very first puzzle, you're pushing a screaming thing around in a cart while it cries in pain and then bashing it out of its shell while it cries in pain, so that you can make it follow you around while it cries in pain. What is it? Who is it? Am I supposed to be stopping its pain or causing more? What's the puzzle? What's the mystery? What's the freaking point?

It's not that I want it handed to the player without earning it; it's that it should exist at some point in the presentation just to feed the pay off, but then there isn't one.

I could go on talking in circles, but that's much of what the game does. It just has you walking in circles. Someone spent a lot of time making detailed and interesting caverns to walk through and filtered it through some atmospheric noise. But beyond the large meaningless puzzle set pieces it's an exercise in futility.

If this game was your Halloween night out, imagine you got all dressed up in a nice costume and then no one bothered to give you any candy. You just walked around your neighborhood while everyone avoided you and slammed their door in your face. And the puzzles were just a maze so you can find your way home disappointed.

Playing this game makes me feel like I went out for Halloween and came back without any candy.

The game is sadly rather disappointing as from playing the game, it seems as if the art and world of the game was created first, and then the story and gameplay was added afterwards. 

Visually, it's a great combination of slzadizalv bekinski and H.R Gieger and brings us a unique, grotesque but intriguing world to explore.
The game has a "biomechanical" feel to everything, and is shown off to great work throughout the game, not to mention that it's HEAVY on the symbolism, that ties into the supposed interpretation of the game. 
One thing it does great, is the gore and bodyhorror, and it does not shy away from showing some genuienly grotesque things, which is shown throughout the game in the enviroment, but also in great animations. 

However the actual gameplay feels tacked on, the gunplay is fine and has punch to it, but is hardly used in the game and still feels clunky and underdeveloped.
The puzzles are never anything but basic and feels more like a blockade for you progress, than a genuine puzzle, in which it requires a button activated. 

The story is left completely open to interpretation, the actual explanation of the things that happends in the game is found inside the artbook, that supposedly don't work anymore.
Moreover the devs themselves have said that some places in the game didn't even make sense to them, and left it open to interpretation to the players, which sounds more like they didn't have a clue on what to 
create for the lore, and just said "let the players figure it out".
It is however one of those games you're left thinking about after you've completed it, either because you found it interesting, or that you're trying to figure out what anything meant.

So, it's hard to recommend the game, when the gameplay is mediocre, the story is pretty much inconsistent and the only thing the game has going for it, is the art.
However, if the game had no gameplay and was merely a simple walking simulator, idon't think a lot of people would have bought it.

Even then all enemies are way too easy to escape that there is almost no point of having any weapons beside the first tool you get, it seems like the developers couldn't decide whether or not to have guns be in the game but eventually were forced to due to the puzzle design and [spoiler] unnecessary end boss fight [/spoiler]. The audio is nice and music is great as expected but the graphics aren't exactly anything to write home about as they are on par with games that came out years ago like Doom or Resident Evil remakes. I feel that if Scorn came out when atmospheric survival horror was more popular it would have been an absolute hit, but this game doesn't do anything defining for that genre gamers haven't already seen.

Overall I can't say I recommend this game, it took me 5 hours to 100% and even on sale for 36$ that is just not worth paying 7$ for each hour of this game and I feel bad for those who have waited years for this. This is a MIXED review. I'm very torn on Scorn, but after considering the pros and cons, I'm more leaning towards giving it a thumbs down now. Do I recommend Scorn at its current price point? No, not really. Do I still think it was a worthwhile journey, and a game you should see? Yes.

Scorn is a one-of-a-kind game, I'll repeat what everybody else said before me and start with a simple fact - the game is absolutely breathtaking visually, and the sound design and atmosphere compliments the graphics in every way possible too. But problem is, that's kinda where I must stop with the positives, because aside of the great artstyle, visuals and sound, Scorn can't really offer much else. 

What I kinda disagree with a lot of other people is the puzzles. I don't think they were bad, actually to me they were the most enjoyable part of the game, what I didn't like was the weird scaling of puzzle difficulty, cuz to me the first hour of the game was by far the hardest and most confusing, even tho I don't believe it was supposed to be. The first puzzle and the first big area were the hardest the game ever was during it's (mind you short) runtime. After the first level it becomes a lot more linear and clear on what you're supposed to do, the puzzles remained fun throughout though I think. So while the difficulty scaling was kinda in reverse, the individual puzzles were fun, not too hard, not too easy.

For me, the game peaked around it's penultimate chapter, I feel like Scorn would've benefitted alot if it extended it's full-geared parts by at least one more level. I felt like it was the most fun when I had all the weapons, scattered and limited resources all around, plenty of creatures to fight and some little problem-solving. Unfortunately, the game doesn't stay in that state for too long, you finish the most dangerous penultimate level, and then it kinda dies out completely. And while the last level is also quite interesting, gameplay-wise it offered some of the most frustrating mechanics which I won't get into, find out for yourselves.

And while we talk about the mechanics, let's touch on the combat. I don't think the combat was as terrible as some claim. It has the typical survival-horror charm. Resources are VERY limited, character movement is very slow and unresponsive, and so is the aiming. The weapons (except the melee one) feel satisfying to use, and I liked the designs. Though my main gripe with the combat was how linear were the scenarios you fight in. Once you've figured how to defeat each enemy type, it was the same everytime you've encountered them, with very little room variety. There's also almost zero opportunity to flee if you think your ammo is low, one of the enemy types in particular is almost impossible to out-maneuver in a tight room cuz your character is so slow. So ultimately I think that's what bothered me the most with the combat, very little creativity to the encounters, and the movement being a tad bit too slow.

The story is also something I didn't quite enjoy. Since there's zero dialogue, zero notes, zero protagonist inner-monologue, zero ANYTHING really, then everything you come up with is a theory, which makes the story ultimately none-existent, as everything comes down to your imagination. So anyone who's claiming there IS a story, is wrong, it's all a theory based on what you see. I think Scorn would've benefitted from at least a little bit of context, at least a flavor text at the beginning or end would help greatly, to at least give some kinda clue on what's happening. Cuz yes, there is environmental storytelling going on, but without anything to go off from, you can't really say anything is set in stone, hence it may aswell be all a dream...

So that's my take on Scorn for now, in the end I give a rare thumbs down on Steam, but I liked my time with it, and I was happy I could support the devs, cuz there's serious potential here for a next, bigger game to come out. They have a talent for artstyle and world design, so now just construct a serious game around it, and we might be cooking here.

For now, only buy it on sale, or if you really wanna experience the world for yourself.

So I really wish I could recommend Scorn. I was excited for it when it was in development and thought the concepts described by the developers were really fascinating. It's rare that you get a biopunk setting and I was hoping this would be a great game to explore that. Unfortunately number of things went wrong. The developers heavily overreached in scope in their planning, not an uncommon thing in indie devs, and had to severely cut down on content. That might be fine if the game itself still made good use of what remained, but most of what's there feels either unfinished or like a rough draft that needed further refinement. 

Most of the game is just wandering around and solving puzzles that you've seen in other games at a pretty dull and laborious pace. The puzzles aren't really interesting and kind of feel out of place in the world they're in with a few exceptions. They feel like something that's more there to slow you down than to expand or explore the world. This is a problem that runs through most elements in the game where it feels like so many of the design choices are centered around stretching out the already thin content and runtime as much as possible.

It also has combat, but it's not really worth talking about. It's slow, clunky, and frustrating. I've heard people say this is intentional as the world is grim and supposed to be difficult and unpleasant, but honestly that feels like an excuse and like people trying to rationalize a bad feature. The mechanics just feel rough and unfinished not intentional. It also forces you into combat so it's not like the game expects you to avoid it. There's a boss near the end that is particularly frustrating and poorly designed. It makes an already slow and tedious game into a slog. 

As for the story... well there is sort of one there, but there isn't much. It's doing some decent visual storytelling about a decaying, cruel, lost culture in a brutal empty world, but there just isn't really any meat there outside of those visual qualities. There are some symbolic attempts towards exploring some themes of abusive and parasitic relationships, but I don't think what is there is very interesting. It seems like there was more planned but a lot got left out when cuts were made so what you get is pretty bare bones. That's in some ways understandable, but it doesn't excuse or make up for the fact that the game just has a very lackluster arc that I don't think says much and is the kind of bleak that feels juvenile rather than insightful. I found myself saying "That's it?" when I reached the finale. 

So I've been tearing into the game pretty heavily here and you might be wondering if there are any bright spots. Luckily there are, even if they have a few blemishes. The visual design is mostly very interesting. The early environmental and creature designs are really good and creative. You can really feel the nature of the world. It has a lot of texture and emotional resonance. Many of the environments feel like exploring a painting and feel fairly unique even if you can clearly see the influence of their inspirations mainly the works of H.R. Giger with a little bit of Zdzisław Beksiński. Personally I wish there was more of the second, but that's a matter of personal taste not quality. This does kind of fall down as the game goes on though as the visual style and design go from being inspired by Giger to just being a direct imitation of his style and works which is disappointing. I wanted to see how the devs explored their own creative themes and style not how well they can imitate another artist. By the end it just feels like you're exploring a knock off Giger sculpture.

So It's glaringly obvious at this point. I don't recommend Scorn as anything but a curiosity purchase. The visual work of the world, creatures, and environments might be worth exploring if you can tolerate the slow and frustrating gameplay. There's also maybe some lessons in scope and game design here to analyze if you're studying or like analyzing game dev. If you can get it on a deep discount, it might be worth it if those qualities interest you. But it's not a game I would recommend anyone play for any kind of real enjoyment. The last bit of salt in the wound is the runtime. I wish I could recommend this game. I really do, I was so excited when I first saw it and I waited so long for it to come out... but it just... fails as a game.  As other reviews have pointed out, the game description is 50% lies. 

First the good,
The game LOOKS great. Well it looks gruesome and awful, but it's very well detailed.  For most of the game I felt I was seeing all unique assets and structures.  The sound is great. Very visceral.

But now the bad.
The combat. The early gameplay trailers made it seem like combat was always a choice. You COULD fight monsters to make your path safer to navigate, but also fighting them was risky and used up some of your already scarce resources. It seemed like sneaking was much more viable. This is not the case in the final game. You either kill the monsters attacking you, or run, trying to dodge their attacks. There is no sneaking. The closest you come is staying out of aggro range until the monster moves out of your way. 

The puzzles. A lot of the puzzles... well they're not the worst but like 90% of the puzzles amount to 'hunt around this environment to find the lever we hid'. Sometimes with the modifier of having to pull the levers in the correct order. They're not good or bad, they're just serviceable.  And for this game to call itself a 'puzzle' game, that is a big failure.

The story. I like implied storytelling. I like having to infer from the world around me. I do not like the story in this game. You have to give me SOMETHING. There is literally no given player character motivation. There is player motivation in the form of "this is a video game, keep moving forward". That doesn't count. Throughout the entire run of the game I was wondering why I was in this place and what I was trying to achieve.  The (spoiler) fact you actually control 2 different characters over the course of the game doesn't help either (it's a very early swap, so barely a spoiler).

The ending. I'm not going to spoil the ending, but I will share my thoughts on it. The ending sucks. It sucks because of the just mentioned story issues. If the game had ended right before solving the final door puzzle (or the final door puzzle could have been solved differently), I would have felt much better about the game. The game honestly could have ended like 5 minutes sooner and have been better for it, because it would have actually given me what the motivation was, even if it was retroactive. But no, the game ended the way it did and destroyed that theory.

Scorn has great visuals, some cool set-pieces, and an interesting atmosphere. Unfortunately, that's all it has going for it. 

There isn't much "exploring" to be done because the game is just a straight line broken up by tedious puzzles. The combat feels like it was added in last minute. Fighting enemies is a pain, and the one boss fight in the game is a slog.

The world doesn't have any substance. It's explicit and disturbing for it's own sake. There's no real story to the game either.  It seems you're meant to interpret whatever deep meaning it has without any context. You could argue that that's the point, but coupled with it's abrupt ending it's ultimately underwhelming.

Finally, this $40 game can be completed in 4-5 hours. It does not give you good value for your money.

If you're willing to look past Scorn's shortcomings for the aesthetic, wait until it's at least 50% off. Otherwise, it's not worth the price tag.

This game is interesting. A ton of thought went into the artstyle and how to make things alien yet still somewhat recognizable as a mechanism with a designed purpose. 
The environments, while somewhat repetitive, are still interesting as each area has its own theme. Its when you spend the entire area walking around nearly identical tunnels that the luster fades until you reach a new area with its own fresh design.
However, there are some issues that leads me to not recommend this game despite 100 percenting it (thought thats not much of an achievement). Firstly, is the false advertising. The store page as of this review, still claims that Scorn is an adventure game with regions that you can explore in a non linear fashion. This game is not non linear. There is only 1 decision point in the entire game and you can reach it in 20 minutes if you can solve the first puzzle pretty quickly. This decision has literally no ramifications on anything once you leave the room outside of which achievement you get. 
The combat is absolutely abysmal. Extremely clunky controls even by the standards of when the game first started development nearly a decade ago, let alone in 2022. Resources are punishingly rare leaidng to the possibilities o being stuck in deathloops, where you walked past a check point with low health forcing you to walk on a knife's edge until you stop dying and find more health. Speaking of checkpoints, their locations are rare, entirely arbitrary, and often many minutes of walking away from where you died, resulting in frequent backtracking to continue the game. No existing method of manual saving. Harping further on this section much longer isn't a good idea, as I can't put my thoughts on that very well. 
Movement around the game world is jerky at best. Character has a very strange level of momentum, though I have heard its much better on controller than keyboard and mouse. There is no jump button. Game is littered with invisible walls to prevent you from exploring too much and is frankly overzealous. In areas where they missed an invisible wall, you will wish they hadnt, because the game does not register fall damage and you will get stuck or fall into the void.
The puzzles are meh. Nuf said.
Overall, a very well done art piece, but not a game I would recommend you play. I recommend watching someone else play, so you can appreciate all the effort that went into visual and audio design while avoiding having to deal with the dreadful gameplay yourself.

The game is visually stunning and I can't name many other games that surpass it in terms of art style. Sadly that's where most of the praises end. Sure it has a fittingly oppressive atmosphere and it provides a niche horror experience, but they really aren't well experienced with gameplay design.

Where the game excels artistically, it falls short with giving the player a fun time alongside it. The combat is geniunely some of the worst I've seen. It's incredibly clunky, sluggish and not rewarding in the slightest. Enemies are more of a chore and annoyance, meant to frustrate the player, than they are a fun and integral part of the game. Honestly, you could've taken them out completely and probably be left with a better, more engaging experience overall. It also doesn't help that you can't tell the recharge on your basic weapon due to the color choice and that same recharge is incredibly slow as is everything else in this game. Not to mention the abhorrent range on that thing. I missed more stuff at near point blank and ended up getting hit back as a result because it's so absurdly short. It also doesn't help that there's little clutter everywhere on the ground that you can easily get stuck on resulting in getting hit more. It only leads to a more frustrating experience. 
And that's not where the shortcomings of the combat end. Switching weapons is also very slow and you can't dodge anything while doing it, so good luck switching to another weapon after running out of ammo mid fight. Also the reloads are slow as hell as is everything else and it's even worse since you can't reload cancel. Once you start reloading, you better believe you're putting every bullet you have into the mag even though you only needed one to finish off the enemy. It also doesn't help that enemies are inconsistent with their health. Sometimes they take 2 shots, sometimes 4. I know it's probably due to the crit spots, but I swear, sometimes I shoot them in the exact same places and they either survive or they just die. This only leads to more unpredictability which can be a detriment to the player and cause more health loss. It really doesn't help that the game is pretty stingy with giving the player healing and that the checkpoints are spaced apart quite a bit.

Apart from that it's also easy to get lost in some of these places. They tend to be quite large, although linear, but most of the areas look the same. Since the game requires quite a bit of backtracking at certain points, you'll be finding yourself blindly searching for where you're supposed to be going. The game doesn't tell the player anything at all. It won't hold your hand and that is completely fine. Sometimes it will leave a better impression if it allows player agency even if it is a linear game, however, it would help if some of the areas weren't so similar looking and maze-like.

The game is also kind of buggy. Sometimes the bullets phase through the enemies, leaving them unaffected. I'm pretty sure the enemies don't have some kind of i-frames, but I could be wrong. Either way it's really annoying missing a shot that clearly hit and then losing precious health because of it. Apart from that, I got stuck in place twice after certain cutscenes for seemingly no reason, resulting in me needing to restart to the latest checkpoint and one time the game didn't allow me to interact with anything even though it was giving me the prompts, leading to another soft lock and reset. It really took away from the overall experience, especially since these bugs were really only a waste of time.

(minor spoilers for the ending) The game is very ambiguous with its story. It doesn't tell you much and only poses more questions than it answers, but it definitely ends with a very negative ending that could be unsatisfying for some, especially because of what you have to go through only to end the game with it. I could bet everyone (myself included) were expecting something very grandiose, but were left disappointed with such a cruel outcome.

Overall, the game has tons of potential, but is too clunky and unsatisfying to play as is. I really do care about it, hence why I'm writing this much. I hope that the developers improve upon the annoyances of this game in their possible future titles and combine such an astounding visual style with good gameplay to form an extremely palatable horror experience.

To put it simply - Scorn is an interesting artistic experience, but an atrocious game to play.
[h1] The good[/h1]
[list]
    [*] This game replicates Giger rather well - everything is disturbingly organic, however if you are underaged or from a puritan family - welp, this isn’t a style for you, as everything has a rather specific… shape.
    [*] Great visuals. While you are in the meaty halls - it is not that obvious, but sometimes the game gives you really nice sceneries.
   [*] Good atmosphere. This is a dead decaying world and you can feel it.
[/list]

[h1] The bad [/h1]
[list]
    [*] Absolutely horrible combat. The enemies are unpleasant to fight as your character moves sluggish and most of the enemies have a ranged attack. They also take too long to deal with. When you get your guns - they take too many bullets from a really limited ammo pool. When you have only a melee tool - well, running into a ranged enemy, making 2 strikes that may or may not kill an enemy, and having to recover the stamina (biotech, in case you forgot) of your tool for 5 seconds mid fight is just a terrible design decision. And unlike the games with good gunplay, Scorn presents its combat more like a puzzle: if you find an ammo refill be prepared to use 90% of said refill on the enemies that will spawn the second you take it, and don’t you dare to miss! The combat is so bad that most of it I wished that Scorn was just a walking sim .
    [*] The puzzles. They aren’t hard, but every single animation takes WAY too long. In fact some of the puzzles have solutions that are obvious in under a minute, but to implement this solution you can waste 10 or more minutes.
    [*] Map layouts/location design. You know how in games you are used to exploring every branching path? And how you are used to finding ammo, collectables or lore in those branches? Forget it, because in Scorn any attempt to go out of your way will be punished by a dead end and a slow way back. This game doesn't have any exploration and even punishes you for attempting to explore. 
    [*] Story. There is none. You can guess the overall events, but it is all left to the player to make sense of the game. And there aren't many things that you can make a story from here - it is just a sightseeing trip but your tour guide is an elitist with a smug face who just offers you to “figure it out” (but in reality he just doesn't have a story to tell).
    [*] The price is too much, both in terms of quality of gameplay, and in terms of quantity. I fully completed the game in 4 hours even though I took my time and didn’t rush.
[/list]
As a conclusion I would rather recommend watching this game on youtube instead of playing it and, god forbid, buying it.

I know it can be hard for developers to digest negative reviews, so I'll try to make this as constructive as possible. 

There is a game-breaking softlock issue in Act 5. This isn't a 'bug'. This softlock is a symptom of the games design. It isn't a weird edge-case and you don't need to think outside of the box to make it happen. Lots and lots of people continue to complain about this gigantic issue that literally breaks your game and stops it in it's tracks. I will explain it in detail: [spoiler] Throughout the game, a parasite that is attached to you regularly drains your health at intervals. You are allowed to refill your health consumable ONCE per health station. In Act 5, you have to fight a boss which essentially consists of three rounds of combat with the same enemy that changes and adapts each time. Prior to this fight, you get to restock your health consumable. So you do the fight and unless this is your second time playing or you're somehow extremely good at this game, you've probably used up your health consumables.[/spoiler]

[spoiler]When you leave the area, the parasite decides it's going to hurt you again. Unlucky players will die here - and will be stuck with no option but to restart the act. But this isn't the 'softlock'. If you manage to survive this cinematic which hurts you (which is a TERRIBLE idea), you become unable to use your hands due to the parasite. To get through the next area, you need to use a device which temporarily destroys the parasite around your hand. This is a gameplay mechanism that is required in order to continue.[/spoiler] 


Now, the softlock: [spoiler]If you beat the boss in Act 5, survived the little cinematic where the parasite hurts you and made it to the hand cruncher AND you only have one bar of health left... you literally cannot finish Scorn. The hand cruncher - the device which is REQUIRED for gameplay progression - hurts you every time you use it. It then hurts you for a set period of seconds afterwards and then the parasite grows back. I couldn't even make it through the door. The nearest health station is beyond a puzzle you must solve - but with one bar of health, you don't have any time to complete the puzzle. You die.[/spoiler]


For those who don't want spoilers / tl;dr - Most players will become locked in Act 5 due to low health and not being able to heal.

Let me be clear: restarting the act isn't a valid fix for this problem. [b]Developers, hear me. You are charging money for this product. It is broken. You need to fix this gigantic problem.[/b] Scorn has lots of problems - and they mostly stem from the unforgiving nature of it's health system (for example: why can't we use health stations repeatedly? It's not a combat centric game. This is a walking puzzle sim.)

Other things that disappointed me:
- The sound would stop working every time the main menu was opened and would only come back when quitting and reloading.

- Zero context is given in regard to the story because there isn't one. Maybe we're supposed to figure it out ourselves, or use our imagination to fill in the blanks, but the problem is it's all blanks. There is no substance, no real plot and no narrative. The world just [i]is[/i]. You are just there doing things [i]because.[/i] The ending [spoiler]is disappointing and explains nothing.[/spoiler]


- Combat is awful and unforgiving. You can't round a corner quickly in Scorn, yet there are enemies that will literally charge at you. Other enemies can spit at you and it's almost like hitscan. There's lots of dissonance in this design. 

- Minimal world cues. I ran around for a long time, getting lost. Maybe that was the intention but it wasn't fun.

It's hard to consume negative reviews - I get it. Scorn has some great scenery, amazing sound design and is overall an intriguing and evocative experience. As a developer myself, I feel like I could make a million suggestions which would elevate it, but the softlock takes the cake. 

This game is broken. You are selling a product with a defect.

EDIT:

Wow this is exploding. I love Dark Souls. Look at my history - I played all three games this year. I can't believe how many people are getting bent out of shape over a game review. I bet you all pre-order your games, don't you? I touched a nerve because I pointed out a problem. Really? They took your money for this, you know. Stop making excuses for the developer.

SCORN was interesting and fun - but I stand by my point. SCORN has a defect. It is broken. Logical gameplay scenarios that lead to dead-ends are called softlocks; and I simply refuse to believe that "just restart the stage bro" is the solution to the softlock I mentioned. For a game about building an immersive world and experience, that's just *terrible*. It's lazy. I will die on this hill. 

People who are saying "git gud" obviously didn't read my review properly. It's not about being 'good enough' to avoid the lock. That is such a dumb, lazy, knee-jerk response. "This player sucks, so they can just get stuck in limbo forever and never complete our game." Rubbish. [/b]

How did the walls decay faster than the bodies? Why do any of the these "Machines" exist? How were the structures erected in the first place? What happened to the world you currently reside in? Why is the parasite an expectation instead of mishap? [spoiler]  Why attempt to go into the "portal" when it's clear none of the other "people" did so? How does the parasite get into that room in the first place? Why can't the object you assume control over not go into the "portal" [/spoiler] And what happened to the person you thought you were at the beginning? 

None of the above questions are answered and it doesn't leave you with a good sense of wonder. It's like nothing in this world has an actual purpose and only exists to prevent you from straight up walking to the ending. The railway was pretty cool but again it doesn't make sense in a functioning world perspective. It seems to just set the conclusion that it is the "end of the line"

Torn on the negative, but even through all the moments where I was stuck in wonder and awe at the visuals and setting, the gameplay itself is atrocious at best and made me not want to finish it several times at worst. 

In the era of Twitch streamers, Let's Players, Vtubers, whatever you want to use to consume your media via watching someone else play through a game, it's the mark of an actually good game where you'll want to play it yourself despite the option to watch someone else play it (or even after doing so) - SCORN is not that. In fact, the only benefit you'd get out of not watching someone else play it, is that you can take your time exploring the environment yourself. And at the end of the experience, I spent maybe 10-20 extra minutes that a content creator wouldn't have admiring the scenery. For 40$. 

In exchange I got to deal with the extremely frustrating combat, where you get absolutely swarmed by enemies in tight hallways with a melee weapon that swings twice with an absurdly long recharge, with only one of the four enemy types in the game being killable in those two swings. Ammo is scarce, even if you can identify the weird looking ammo stations in the winding areas you'll be constantly walking through as most of it kind of blends together. Movement during combat is lackluster, as you move slow, even when sprinting. Reloading or changing your weapon slows you down even further. Catching on the terrain constantly in these tight hallways was an additional nuisance. Enemies have near pinpoint accuracy with their ranged attacks or in the case of the big chargers, charge you relentlessly (and stunlock you when you get hit). Several times I died because I was simply cornered and couldn't get around what was attacking me. Each time I died I considered uninstalling and not finishing the game.

There was a lot of complaints about puzzles, but as I have a slightly above room temperature IQ I didn't find them too bad. Lots of trial and error got me through them relatively quickly. And again. Four hours for the total experience.

If ammo had been more plentiful, or combat was more responsive, if killing the myriad repeat enemies was satisfying in any way shape or form, then I could easily recommend SCORN. It's an experience that left me with questions and an appreciation for the artistry of the setting. Hell, if the game had been a walking simulator, I still think it would have been worth buying, simply because of how unique it is. But unfortunately, the gameplay left it feeling like there was a lot of wasted potential and as a result I cannot recommend SCORN.

Close call deciding to rate this positive or negative. I had basically been waiting for a game like this to come out ever since I saw Alien as a kid and watching my dad play Dead Space. It has everything I ever wanted in terms of aesthetic and body horror elements which is something that affects me greatly, even when it comes to small things. I'm the type of person that can get nauseous just from someone talking about blood, guts, or surgery... things of that sort, so I guess you could say I have a fear of offal. And yes, I became very, very, very, very nauseous in the late-game...

Unfortunately, all of these sentiments are held back by the sometimes rage-inducing parts of this game that highlight a staggeringly simplistic gameplay loop. The first issue I can see that ruins any fear or anxiety a player might have coming into this is the combat and limited number of enemy types. It is laughable that after fighting the first actual foe the game throws at you, you already know how to cheese the rest of the enemies in the game. How am I supposed to be scared of something once I realize I can just strafe around it in a circles while it helplessly misses every attack? Not to mention that I was pretty liberal with my heals and ammo and still had a surplus, the exact opposite of the claim that players will have to choose their battles to progress. Another issue tied with this is that the "combat" portion of the game has a significant bulk to it, and its length further exposes how bad the gunplay is. Also, the only normal "boss" the game has is one of the worst designed bosses I have ever fought, and was the only time I died during my playthrough. Thankfully so, as I have heard rumors that the save system is piss-poor so it seems my run could have been a much greater headache.

Despite all of this, for me I believe I took a net positive experience from this. I can say with satisfaction that there wasn't a moment during my run that I was bored, as every time that I wasn't directly progressing I was absorbed in the architecture and ambient sounds that the levels provide. In some weird twisted way the world almost becomes relaxing as you get used to the sights and sounds. If you still decide to pick up Scorn do so knowing that I personally only enjoyed it because I had a pre-established fascination with H.R. Giger and body horror like I said before, so gauge if this is money well spent for YOU.

So... yeah I really wanted to like this game. I did.
But I can't stand it.
It's weirdly beautiful, sure.  It's innovative in areas like the very 'unique...?'  inventory system.  Cool.  So without going all in on this one, let's just drill it out:
* This is a puzzle game. Not a shooter.  My mistake.  
* The puzzles are obnoxious, notably the first one.  There is practically no context for the clues given.  Some of the items you have to perform.  I don't use strategy guides, so it probably took longer for me than others.  But yeah.  I hated them.  Most of the puzzles are deliberately obtuse.
* There is no context. For anything. Anywhere.  You bumble around, slowly, finding your way through the environment.  Sure, it gives a bit of the sense of what the character would feel, but it ends up being tiresome.
* The weapons... suck. They are godawful.  The melee attack 'gun' does pitiful damage and is hard to use.  The pistol requires line up time while they zap you with spit.  They never do quite enough damage.  
* Everything - EVERYTHING has a 5-10 second animation.  It's cool, the first time.  Then when you go to reload, or use an elevator, or whatever - it's the same animation.  Every time.  Over and over. 
* There's no plot.  At all.  It's obviously designed to give a sense of ambiguity, but there's ambiguity and then there's just... nothing.  This is the latter.
* It's just... not fun.  I don't know any other way to put it.  Playing the game is a chore.  It's not fun.  You constantly just feel punished by existing, which is probably what they were going for - but it's not something you actively want to do unless you're a masochist. 
Little annoyances:
* No quicksave
* No secrets
* No difficulty level(s)
* No reward at all for playing.  Unless you like numbered photographs as 'achievements'.

I realize this is pretty harsh and unforgiving - but this is to spare you the agony of playing this game. I literally decided to go CLEAN MY KITCHEN than continue.  That's how much I began to hate it.  Will I go and spite-finish it later? Absolutely.  But that's not an indication of enjoyment. It's an indication I hate wasting money.  I'm going to spite-finish this game and then never touch it again.  Do yourself a favor and just avoid that and just.. never touch it.
